Question Text: Tom is a Servant leader of a complex software development project that is running using Agile development approach. Two developers are having difference in opinion about the technical approach of a user story. What needs to be done in this situation?
Selected Answer: Tom should assess the level of conflict and intervene appropriately
Correct Answer: Entire team should gather to discus the issue and produce a collective solution
Feedback: On an empowered agile team, it's up to the team members to resolve their technical disputes collectively. The scrum master, or the product owner is unlikely to have the knowledge required to make such technical decisions. So, among all options, option C is the best answer. Agile Practice Guide - Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) – 41-43, 61.

Question Text: The project team is using Iteration burn-down chart to predict the remaining work in the current iteration backlog. Iteration Burn-down chart is an example of which of the following tools and techniques?
Correct Answer: Data Analysis
Feedback: The burn-down chart is an example for data analysis tool that shows the total effort against the amount of work for each iteration. PMBOK Guide – Sixth Edition, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) – 226 & 687.

Question Text: A newly formed development team is started writing user stories after an understanding of the features and functions. The few examples of user stories are as follows: Users can make reservations so that they can travel Show room sizes so that they can see if it fits their need . Which one of the following problem would you like to fix in these user stories?
Selected Answer: The user stories are not explored from the user value point of view
Correct Answer: The user stories are not clarifying the specific users
Feedback: The user value is mentioned in these user stories. In first user story user wants to travel and in second user story users are visualizing value through their specific room size requirements. The estimates depend on size of user stories and question is not indicating that team has estimated these user stories as big in size. The user story is just a token of conversation and collaboration and writing acceptance criteria makes user stories testable. Above description eliminates following options: The user stories are not explored from the user value point of view The user stories are not small enough to estimate The user stories are not testable In these examples we can see development team is not mentioning the specific user roles – it is an important component of a user stories. Without specific intended user the identified value is vague and we are not aware who will benefit from it. If you are not aware about real user stories, then it is not right time to write user stories, first identify user roles like Student, Job seeker Employer for a Job Portal.

Question Text: A Release burndown chart is showing burn up, what could be the possible reason?
Selected Answer: The team is not delivering stories as per estimated velocity
Correct Answer: When new stories are added to release backlog.
Feedback: When additional work is added to a release , the team working with its normal velocity end up with more story points left at the end of iteration than they began working with.

Question Text: A permanent highly skilled staff hired for the project to avoid potential budget overruns. However, there is a risk of staff turnover during  the  course of the project, which may have an impact on the delivery. Which two actions should the project manager take to mitigate this risk? Choose two
Selected Answer: Introduce a recognition program to motivate and reward and reward resource performance. Increase the trained staff to create back up for resources.
Correct Answer: Introduce a recognition program to motivate and reward and reward resource performance. Increase the trained staff to create back up for resources.
Feedback: Two actions are: Increase the trained staff to create back up for resources and introduce a recognition program to motivate and reward resource performance.

Question Text: Which of the following is not an example of the four values of the Agile Manifesto?
Selected Answer: Working software is the primary measure of progress
Correct Answer: Working software is the primary measure of progress
Feedback: The options - A, C, D falls under four values of the Agile manifesto. Option B is an example for one of the twelve Agile principles behind the Agile manifesto. So, among all options, option B is the right answer. Agile Practice Guide - Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) – 8,9.

Question Text: Tom is the newly appointed Project Manager of a software development project which has high degree of uncertainties and scope is not yet fully defined. Considering all the factors, he decides to adopt Agile development approach for running the project. Now, he has to come up with an initial cost estimate before the project work begins. What can be the best approach for the preparation of initial cost estimate as per the stated scenario?
Selected Answer: Using Analogous estimation technique to produce a high-level cost estimate
Correct Answer: Using light weight estimation methods to generate a high-level cost forecast.
Feedback: Projects with a high degree of uncertainty or if the scope is not fully defined may not benefit from detailed cost calculations because there are frequent changes. In an agile environment, lightweight estimates can be used to generate a high-level cost of project labor costs, which can be adjusted when changes are made. (PMBOK Guide) – Sixth Edition, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) – 234.

Question Text: Match the term with its corresponding description.

Todd is a project manager of a very large software product development project that needs to be executed from five different cities. Senior management has decided to run the project using an agile approach by following the philosophies of the scrum as much as possible. What framework is most suited as per the given situation?
Correct Answer: LeSS
Feedback: The situation in the question states about a very large project that needs to be executed using an agile approach by following the philosophies of the scrum. LeSS (Large Scale Scrum) is a framework that extends Scrum with scaling guidelines while preserving the original purposes of Scrum. It's most applicable for many teams (cross-functional) working together on one product. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 20-23

Question Text: A team member shares with their functional manager some negative details about the performance of another team member that was discussed during the retrospective. The project manager finds out about this discussion. What two actions should the project manager take? Choose two.
Selected Answer: Meet with the entire team to review the ground rules about safe environments. Contact with the team member to explain what information can be shared outside the team.
Correct Answer: Meet with the entire team to review the ground rules about safe environments. Contact with the team member to explain what information can be shared outside the team.
Feedback: 1- Contact the team member to explain what information can be shared outside the team. 2- Meet with the entire team to review the ground rules about safe environments.

Question Text: At a walkthrough, a stakeholder, end user, and the development team identify significant new functionality required for the proposed solution to be effective. What is the next step?
Selected Answer: The new functionality should be added to the product backlog.
Correct Answer: The new functionality should be added to the product backlog.
Feedback: In agile, the development team commits to a group of user stories at the beginning of an iteration. Likewise, the product owner agrees not to disrupt the team during this timebox. For this reason, the best answer is that the new functionality should be added to the product backlog, to be estimated and prioritized later. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 52-53

Question Text: Stakeholders want to understand what progress an agile team has made in their last iteration. What should stakeholders review to determine this information?
Correct Answer: The team's velocity chart
Feedback: The results of a spike would show team findings on a specific issue. A product backlog is a list of items to be developed for the project. In agile, 'fishbone analysis' is a genuine technique and one can 'slice' up user stories. However, combined 'fishbone slices' is a made-up term. Velocity charts show how much work the team has completed in each iteration. For each iteration, a velocity chart shows the amount of work completed . Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 64

Question Text: As an Agile Coach, what is the BEST way for you to handle a complex situation during a delivery?
Selected Answer: Allow the team to self-manage & adapt its process empirically
Correct Answer: Allow the team to self-manage & adapt its process empirically
Feedback: The Agile project manager should allow the team to self-manage & adjust its process as the team deems appropriate.

Question Text: Which of the following represents the purpose of Sprint review Meeting BEST?
Selected Answer: Team to present to the Product Owner and stakeholders functionality that is done
Correct Answer: Team to present to the Product Owner and stakeholders functionality that is done
Feedback: The purpose of the Sprint review is for the Team to present to the Product Owner and stakeholders functionality that is done.

Question Text: Members of the team post updates to a graph that shows the progression of features to being 'Done.' Examples of the stages of progress include Backlog, Design, Development, Testing and Done. What is the name of this graph?
Correct Answer: Cumulative flow diagram
Feedback: A cumulative flow diagram depicts the progression of a set of features from start to finish. It's a Kanban way of monitoring work; Burndown chart does not reflect the stages of work.

Question Text: How does release plan help?
Correct Answer: Helps in understanding of the project's viability.
Feedback: Release plans helps in developing a better understanding of the project's viability.

Question Text: Which approach is BEST for estimating Agile Projects while doing the release planning?
Correct Answer: Top down approach.
Feedback: A top down approach is used when estimating Agile Projects at the release level, as it is impossible to predict the work with any degree of certainty at the task level.

Question Text: During an iteration planning meeting, the team is estimating the size of the effort for each story by assigning each story to a shirt size of XS, S, M, L, XL or XXL. Which estimation method is being used?
Correct Answer: Affinity estimating
Feedback: The estimating scenario described here is affinity estimating. As we are grouping the stories in affinity for estimation purpose.

Question Text: The ongoing sprint for a software development project that is being executed by following Agile - Scrum development approach needs to be cancelled as the sprint goal has become obsolete due to a sudden change in law associated to IT security.Who will own the Product backlog?
Correct Answer: Product Owner.
Feedback: The product owner is responsible for maximizing the value of the product, and only he has authority to cancel the sprint, although he or she may do under the influence from key stakeholders, sponsor, project manager or any other stakeholders A sprint gets cancelled when sprint goal becomes obsolete due to sudden change associated to organizational policies, external environmental factors or due to any adverse situations impacting the project. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 101

Question Text: The Scrum Master explains the three primary roles in Scrum to the newly hired team member. Which role is sometimes called 'the voice of the customer'?
Correct Answer: Product owner
Feedback: The product owner is defined as the "individual who serves as the voice of the customer, and who has the authority to make decision about the product. "The product owner is responsible for bridging the gaps between the customer, business stakeholders, and the development team. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 41

Question Text: An agile practitioner is explaining the Agile Manifesto to some end users in advance of a new project. Which of the following would the agile practitioner say is preferred in an agile project?
Correct Answer: Collaborating with customers
Feedback: The Agile Manifesto lays out four values. Collaborating with the customer is preferable to contract negotiation. Likewise, individuals and interactions are valued more than processes and tools. Responding to change is more valued than following a plan, and working software is preferred over documentation. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 8

Question Text: In a typical business complex and mid-sized agile project, what does the team attempt to develop every Sprint?
Correct Answer: A Potentially Releasable Product Increment
Feedback: The output of every Sprint is called a Potentially Releasable Product Increment. It is the sum of the Product Backlog Items completed during a Sprint. Delivering Potentially Releasable Product each Sprint is fundamental to the Scrum since in agile as work is divided into simple pieces, it can be finished in a short iteration. The product backlog is a living document that has anything and everything about project work. It is the ordered list of all the work presented in story form for a team Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 101

Question Text: The product owner of an agile project has the responsibility of grooming the product backlog. Grooming involves prioritizing and re-prioritizing user stories on a regular basis. As an agile best practice, which of the following criteria are most important for the owner to use when grooming the product backlog?
Correct Answer: Customer value and risk
Feedback: The two most important criteria to consider when the product owner is grooming the product backlog is the value of the user story and the risk involved in the work required to complete the user story. High-value user stories are always considered high priority. High-risk user stories are typically prioritized so that the risk of project failure can be dealt with or determined early in the project before significant costs and resources have been devoted. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 52-53

Question Text: A scrum team that has been working on an agile project, is arguing over the story points in the sprint meeting planning. The product owner is pushing the team to complete 170 story points of user stories in the next sprint whereas the average velocity of the development team is 150 story points per sprint. Who will make the final decision to fix the number of story points to be completed in a sprint?
Correct Answer: The development teams
Feedback: In the scrum, before making any commitment about the completion of user stories, development team discusses and then decides how many story points they can complete in the current sprint. It is the development team that is going to work on the product and know their capability and pace, therefore, the development team should make the final decision to fix the number of story points to be completed in a sprint.

Question Text: Which of the following is not a feature of an Agile team?
Correct Answer: Each team member has a specialty
Feedback: An agile team is a cross-functional team. They are preferred to be a generalist. A cross-functional team is one with a variety of skills, abilities and experience, so that they can develop their scope (stories, features, "product backlog items", whatever) by themselves, without help from others.

Question Text: On the completion of the first three iterations, an agile team determined that 344 story points are required to complete the remaining project. The average team velocity in the first three iterations was 50 story points. What will be the number of iterations required for the team to complete the project?
Correct Answer: 7 Iterations
Feedback: The velocity of the team is used to track the progress of the project and measured in terms of how many user stories it completes in one iteration. The average velocity of the team is measured based on its performance in the first few iterations .In this question, the average team velocity in the first three iterations was 50 story points. Now, 344 story points are left to complete the project. The number of iterations required to complete the project is calculated as the number of story points left divided by the average team velocity i.e. 344/50 in this case. It calculates at 6.88. In the case of iterations, we need to consider the whole number next to the result. Therefore, there is a need for 7 more iterations to complete the project.

Question Text: A team member is constantly spending on items that are not in the sprint backlog. As a Scrum Master what should you do?
Selected Answer: Talk to the member in person.
Correct Answer: Talk to the member in person.
Feedback: As a first step, Scrum Master should talk to the member in person to understand the situation better. Only if needed, the issue may be further discussed with the team.

Question Text: Florian is a stakeholder in STC company. He has recently learned that the team will use an agile framework in the current project. In a planning meeting, Florian tells the team members that they are not doing formal documentation in this project as they were doing in the previous projects. How will the team members reply to his statement?
Selected Answer: In agile, documentation is done for the clear work item only
Correct Answer: In agile Methodology, The documentation is kept barely sufficient to fulfill regulatory requirement
Feedback: Agile Manifesto Value number 2 states "Working software over comprehensive documentation". In agile, creating the formal documentation with a detailed description of everything is considered a wastage of time. It does not mean that documentation is not necessary at all. It is necessary but it should be kept barely sufficient to fulfill regulatory requirements in an agile environment. Although for some safety-critical products, some additional documentation and conformance checks are recommended.

Question Text: The velocity of an 8-member Agile team over the past few sprints has been 36, 32, 40, 46, 38 and 48 story points. In the next 2-week Sprint, there are two public holidays planned. How many points must the team plan for?
Correct Answer: Whatever the team feel comfortable with
Feedback: The historical velocity is only a 'guideline' for future sprint planning – it is not a 'must' . The final decision on exactly how many points are picked up for the next Sprint rests with the team.

Question Text: One role of an agile practitioner is to promote the knowledge and execution of agile practices within an organization. Which of the following agile practitioners is responsible for the creation and maintenance of the product roadmap?
Correct Answer: Product owner
Feedback: The product owner is the voice of the customer and has the information and access required to define and prioritize development iterations, releases and ultimately a product roadmap. Once created the product owner is responsible for any changes required to the product roadmap and the individual releases that collectively form the roadmap. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 41

Question Text: A team lead is currently demonstrating a potentially shippable product increment for project stakeholders. Which agile meeting is being conducted?
Correct Answer: Iteration review meeting
Feedback: At the end of each iteration, the project team demonstrates a potentially shippable product increment to project stakeholders during the iteration review meeting. These meetings may also be referred to as demonstrations or sprint reviews. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 55

Question Text: At the sprint retrospective meeting, the team lead drew a fishbone diagram, wrote a problem at the head of the fish, and labeled the bones of the fish with categories. What should the team do next?
Correct Answer: Brainstorm factors within each category
Feedback: After the problem is written at the head of the fish, and after the bones of the fish are labeled with categories, the next step is to brainstorm factors within each category. A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge, (PMBOK® Guide) – Sixth Edition., 2017, Page(s), 293-294

Question Text: What is the most important reason why Product Owner needs to be present in Sprint Planning meeting?
Selected Answer: Decide team velocity based on historical performance
Correct Answer: Provide clarification on requirements
Feedback: Providing details on requirements is the most important reason PO needs to attend Sprint Planning meeting. Other three tasks need to be performed by the team.

Question Text: Team has finished release planning meeting and agreed on condition of satisfaction, priority of backlog items, team velocity, etc. There are some large features that were not estimated, however team decided to split them closer to development. Few sprints have passed, but team has not been able to update release plan due to time constraints. During Sprint Planning, team decides to split one large feature into 4 smaller stories based on operational boundaries. Unfortunately, there is not enough capacity in the current iteration, so team can include only 2 of the 4 stories in this sprint. When team demonstrates the product increment during the sprint review meeting, the PO refuses to accept these two user stories that the team had marked as Done. What could have potentially gone wrong?
Selected Answer: During Sprint planning meeting, condition of satisfaction or acceptance criteria may not have been discussed while splitting the user story.
Correct Answer: During Sprint planning meeting, condition of satisfaction or acceptance criteria may not have been discussed while splitting the user story.
Feedback: Conditions-of-satisfactions are continuously iterated, They are discussed and agreed upon, both at the start of release planning and iteration planning. In the question above the most likely scenario for PO not accepting the stories during Demo is that condition of the satisfaction of each of the user story derived by splitting feature, would have not been discussed. Since not all the user stories that comprised the feature were part of sprint it is even more important that definition of done is discussed for each story and not rely on definition of done for the feature which was agreed during release planning meeting. Team can split features based on operational boundaries, Release plan should be periodically revisited and revised however that is not the reason for problem, The definition of done is orthogonal to user acceptance criteria (functional acceptance) for a feature. It is a comprehensive checklist of necessary, value-added activities that assert the quality of a feature and not the functionality of that feature/story.

Question Text: How does an agile team go about developing a schedule?
Selected Answer: By estimating story points and making use of the team velocity
Correct Answer: By estimating story points and making use of the team velocity
Feedback: The team estimates story points and applies the team velocity (the rate at which the team completes story points), and derives a schedule.

Question Text: What role Product Owner plays in the sprint planning meeting?
Selected Answer: Product Owner grooms or maintains the Product Backlog and prioritized stories are used for sprint planning
Correct Answer: Product Owner grooms or maintains the Product Backlog and prioritized stories are used for sprint planning
Feedback: B is the best choice of the 4. The Product Owner creates and maintains the backlog for the product, therefore, the Product Owner directs the team activities by prioritize items in the backlog based on the anticipated value of each item.

Question Text: In evaluating an agile project, which of the following metrics would you use to compare effectiveness of two agile team / projects?
Correct Answer: Return on investment
Feedback: Agile recommends making people accountable for customer outcomes. Velocity is good for release planning but not for comparing two teams. You may think that Return on Investment goes beyond the scope of the team but it is not, the product owner and the team have to work on generating maximum value not high velocity.

Question Text: An agile team finished coding for the current iteration. Which of the following is a continuous process improvement ceremony that the team will now attend?
Correct Answer: Iteration retrospective meeting
Feedback: The iteration retrospective meeting is a formal ceremony used in agile. This event is held at the end of each iteration where lessons learned during the iteration are reviewed, and specific plans of action are implemented during the next iteration to prevent these issues from occurring again on the project. Agile Practice Guide, Project Management Institute Inc., 2017, Page(s) 50-51

Question Text: While working on a hybrid project, an agile practitioner is responsible to perform the duties of both the project scrum master and provide project performance reports periodically to the senior management. The project sponsor suggests the agile practitioner that track the velocity of each team member individually instead of tracking the team velocity to monitor the progress of the project. What would the agile practitioner do as per agile best practices?
Selected Answer: Track and report only individual velocity to monitor the team performance
Correct Answer: Track and report only team velocity to monitor the team performance
Feedback: Agile best practices prefer to track and report the velocity of the team rather than the individual's velocity for monitoring the project. But some agile teams track the velocity of each team member individually in terms of completed story points or ideal days. This is not a good approach as it can cause behavioral issues in the team and can work against the success of the project team.

Question Text: Which two actions should a project manager consider while launching a new virtual team? (choose two)
Selected Answer: Verify if team member's own strengths and weaknesses as a virtual team leader to identify avoidable pitfalls
Correct Answer: Establish in the beginning, bow progress will be monitored and the means for communicating progress. Verify if team members are on more than one team and cannot devote enough time to this team.
Feedback: 1- Establish in the beginning, how progress will be monitored and the best means for communicating progress. 2- Verify if team members are on more than one team and cannot devote enough time to this team.
